title: Paternal-line comparisons
dataset_scope: 23 saved Y67 tester observations, plus one separate A823 comparator. These are observation rows, not 23 independently documented paternal families. No fresh account data were read for this table; primary comparison-reading dates are retained per link.
interpretation_rules: Exclusions apply to the specific observed typed lines, never to every family with the surname.
Repeated testers, surname spellings and nested branches are not independent confirmations. No independent-family count is established.
Official Y67 GD, extended STR differences, single-copy lower bounds and SNP differences are different measures; only official same-level Y67 GD appears in that column.
A close STR distance cannot establish recentness. Broad placement, no-call or absent match-list entry is not a negative genotype.
McMaster/McMasters separation retains qualitative read-view limits; it is not calibrated raw sequence QC.
No surname probabilities, precise pairwise dates, former-surname direction, Aaron-level genetic assignment or confidence change is supplied. An untested family remains possible.

dependency_groups.reason: Shared downstream McMaster/McMasters path; two terminal assignments. Three observations do not establish three independent paternal families.
Kelly's saved path includes Brown's BY76755 branch. Different surname labels are not independent branch evidence; documentary relationship remains unknown.
McCormack's saved path descends through McCormick's BY81068 branch. Broader shared placement is not independent-family proof.

documentary_cross_reference.scope: A bounded cross-check of the saved research corpus and selected previously acquired originals, completed 2 October 2026. Nine historical surname entries cover the nine unresolved Y67 observations plus the distinct A823 DeVenney comparator. No fresh external discovery query, archive-wide search or all-surname inventory was completed. Historical record dates and prior reading scopes are retained in each entry.
methodology: Use the recorded spelling, date, place and role. Listed search forms are discovery vocabulary; they do not establish that differently named people share a family. Devine/Divine, McCain, Burns and Carrell require their own identity evidence. Oliphant, Olliphant, Olyphant, Olifant, Olifent, Oliphint and Olliphint are discovery forms for future source searches; the younger marriage’s recorded form is Aaron Olifant Devany, not a normalized replacement.

The strongest named-local lead is the younger Aaron Olifant Devany in Hancock decades after the elder Aaron. His name, county and enumeration association do not prove kinship or connect him to either distinct DNA comparator.

Government execution, an officiant’s name and a possible parcel predecessor are different kinds of association. A routine official signature is weak family evidence; reconstruct a named personal relationship before assigning ancestry.

Hancock and Greene named records provide the core comparison anchors. Earlier Pendleton appearances retain same-person limits; the Rutherford witness’s identity remains unresolved. A record made in one county can state residence in another.

Rank the next documentary test within this finite screen, not the likelihood of an ancestral surname. Preserve DNA status separately. Failure to locate a connection in saved material does not exclude the surname or imply that the relevant records were exhaustively searched.

evidence.label: Hancock marriage, 14 January 1866: Aaron Olifant Devany and Martha Andrews
evidence.scope: p. 104; DGS 5190837, image 174. License 13 January; marriage return 14 January 1866. Full name and marriage established. Previously read 28 September; saved original locally reinspected 2 October 2026.

evidence.label: Hancock enumeration, 16 June 1870: Humphrey, A. O. and Drury households
evidence.scope: p. 31, stamped 436: dwellings/families 271/278, 273/280 and 275/282, with intervening households. Enumeration association only. Previously read 28 September; saved original locally reinspected 2 October 2026.

evidence.label: Elder Aaron's stated Hancock residence, 29 January 1821
evidence.scope: Pendleton Book P, p. 382. Calls Aaron of Hancock County and identifies wife Rebecca as deceased Solomon Rainwater’s daughter. Previously read 28 September; saved original locally reinspected 2 October 2026.

evidence.label: N02: namesake evidence, conflicting identities and completed coverage
evidence.scope: Existing public synthesis dated 30 September 2026; read from the current saved report on 2 October. No fresh repository acquisition or access check.

rows.limits: A later full name and same county supply a specific lead, with no demonstrated kinship to elder Aaron or explanation for the name. Enumeration order proves neither adjoining land nor family relationship. Parents and Drury relationship remain unresolved. FL02's broad Y67 GD5 comparison and FL24's separate A823 comparison are different testers; neither has a documented descent to this historical family. No surname-transition or historical Y-line conclusion follows.
rows.next_test: Seek an explicit parent, sibling, guardian, heir or naming statement. Await the existing Richmond request for William A. Davaney’s temporary letters (book 7, p. 175), permanent letters (book 14, p. 89) and associated estate papers (COR11/N23). Verify estate and nephew identities before using kinship wording. Do not repeat the completed broad 1860 and guardian/index screens without a new discriminator.

rows.priority: Low: official execution and unresolved secondary readings

evidence.label: Aaron's Appling grant, 4 March 1824, p. 63
evidence.scope: Elisha Wood, S.E.D., appears in the official execution of the recorded grant naming Aaron Olliphant of Sharp's district, Hancock County. The saved original was reread on 2 October. This is an official role, not demonstrated personal contact, kinship or an identified Wood comparison lineage.

evidence.label: N26: neighboring parcels and the grant-name conflict
evidence.scope: The separate 50-acre Knight/Harden/Gentry parcel reads Mathew Good in 1818 and Matthew Wood in 1823. The underlying grant remains unverified. This parcel is distinct from Aaron's 230-acre bond tract. Jonathan Woodard/Woodward is a documented bond party, but his surname is not automatically Wood.

rows.limits: No documented link to the FL05 paternal family. The later Celia Wood statement in a Devany death certificate belongs to a separate, incompletely linked namesake-family investigation. Official execution, the Good/Wood conflict and Woodard must not be counted as three independent Wood-family links.
rows.next_test: Require a named personal or family connection before extending the historical Wood lead; verify the original grant behind the Good/Wood conflict only if it becomes discriminating. Resolve the correctly identified comparison's finer SNP placement separately.

rows.priority: Low: separate McCain lead outside Aaron's documented anchors

evidence.label: Sarah Dalton temporary administration, 22 April 1826, p. 55
evidence.scope: William McCain administered Sarah Dalton's estate in Richmond County. The saved original-source review records the abbreviated Mc surname and no stated relationship. This is a separate surname and an indirect Dalton candidate trail, rather than an Aaron transaction in Hancock, Greene, Pendleton or Rutherford. The saved original was previously read 29 September 2026; this cross-reference uses that dated review rather than a fresh reading.

evidence.label: N23: Dalton notices and bounded probate coverage
evidence.scope: The notices name no Polly, Samuel, Charlotte, Devaney or Oliphant; the supposed Sarah Dalton estate account was corrected to Sabra Dawson. No bridge from this McCain to Aaron or the Cain comparison was established.

rows.limits: No named Cain-family intersection with Aaron was identified in the examined saved corpus. McCain is a discovery possibility, not an established Cain variant. A separate 1795 Laurens Cain boundary context involving James Oliphant is outside the stated anchors and lacks an Aaron bridge. Cane Creek is a place-name, not a surname hit. This is not a county-wide or archival negative.
rows.next_test: Pursue McCain only after a named Dalton-to-Aaron bridge or independent evidence of surname identity appears. Otherwise obtain the identified comparison's finer SNP evidence and a documented paternal route before broad pedigree expansion.

evidence.scope: Existing project coverage was reviewed before the local historical-name screen. Scotland and other project members' Dumfries labels are submitted pedigree or group context; they do not establish a historical McCubbin family in Aaron's documented places.

rows.limits: No named McCubbin-form connection to Aaron or an identified associate was found in the examined saved Markdown corpus. Attachments, unindexed manuscripts and complete county record series were not exhaustively screened. This does not exclude a historical connection or supply a negative finer SNP call.
rows.next_test: Require a named historical person with a dated transaction, relationship or migration bridge into Aaron's anchors; verify comparison identity and finer SNP placement before building a Scotland pedigree.

evidence.label: John and Martha Rainwater pension selection, PDF p. 11
evidence.scope: Samuel and Polly Bowen's 1851 Anderson affidavit says they believed John Rainwater and Martha Adams were married on 14 March 1815 by M. Collins, a regular ordained minister. The saved p. 11 original image was reread on 2 October. It is retrospective testimony about a marriage, not a contemporary Collins/Aaron transaction.

evidence.label: N57: Rainwater military and migration context
evidence.scope: The Rainwater pension narrative supplies a Pendleton-Hancock-Greene route and a Nash-regiment context worth correlating with Aaron. Identification of this pensioner with Aaron's estate associate remains qualified; the officiant is an additional indirect name, not an Aaron relative.

rows.limits: The affidavit says M. Collins, not an expanded given name. No relationship to Aaron or to FL22's paternal family is documented. A separate saved Aaron Collins machine-text hit was rejected as an apparent transcription artifact. County-level Collins presence and a reported officiant role cannot repair missing comparison identity/SNP evidence.
rows.next_test: Seek a contemporary marriage/church record that identifies the specific minister and couple if this network becomes discriminating. Require a personal Aaron bridge and independently documented paternal route before promoting the surname.

rows.priority: Targeted parcel lead; surname identity remains unproved

evidence.label: Carrell to Leonard Shockley, 25 October 1811, pp. 143-144
evidence.scope: Harvel/Harwel A. Carrell of Hancock conveyed 230 acres in Greene and Hancock on Shoulderbone to Leonard Shockley of Greene. The saved p. 144 original was reread on 2 October. Its ordered Pole-branch/Mapp/S55E/S35W description strongly corresponds to the later 1822/1830 tract sequence associated, with limits, with Aaron's 1825 bond. The recorded spelling remains Carrell.

evidence.label: N26: incomplete 230-acre title chain
evidence.scope: The 1825 bond names James Harden as occupant; his 1822 acquisition matches the 1830 Woodward/Barnes description. Leonard-to-Michael L. Shockley and Hardin-to-Woodard transfers remain unlocated, and the 1811 deed itself does not name Aaron.

rows.limits: This is an earlier parcel party, not a demonstrated personal associate or relative of Aaron. Carrell has not been identified as Carroll or McCarroll, and dropping the Mc prefix is only a discovery possibility. No link to FL23's paternal family or any surname transition follows.
rows.next_test: Close the two missing interests in the specific 230-acre title chain or find an explicit Carrell/Aaron record. Require source evidence for a Carrell-to-McCarroll identity before expanding that surname pedigree.
